description: The abdominal wall is skin, a variable layer of subcutaneous fat and the rectus sheath and flat muscles; deep to it lies the peritoneal cavity with the bowel. Under the right costal margin the liver, under the left the spleen and stomach; behind the bowel, in the midline, the aorta and inferior vena cava; above the pubis a full bladder. In the groin the femoral nerve, artery and vein lie side by side (lateral to medial) under the inguinal crease, the artery at the mid-inguinal point; the inferior epigastric vessels run up behind the rectus muscles.

review.notes: Depths below the skin of the lungs, organs, bones and great vessels are measured on one reference body (a 38-year-old man of about 90 kg) and scaled to each patient by height and BMI; the rest is schematic. Not a guide to safe depths in real patients. Anatomical expert review is required before any teaching use.

provenance.notes: Depth grid (2.5 cm): the wall's thickness and the depths of liver, spleen, kidneys, bowel, bladder, aorta and venae cavae are measured by rays on the reference body; the fat/muscle split of the wall and the groin vessels, nerve and inferior epigastric artery are schematic. The stomach is absent from the reference body: under the upper abdomen the first viscus measured may be the liver, pancreas or colon.
